full_judgment:
6. The petitioner has filed an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1907 for condonation of delay of 4132 days in filing the appeal. On the basis of this application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, Rule was issued on 12-7-2005 and the matter has been taken up for hearing. 

 7. Beard the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner and the learned Assistant Attorney-General for the State and perused the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act along with supplementary affidavit for condoning the delay of 4132 days in filing the appeal. 

 15. In the instant case it is an admitted fact that the trial was held in absentia. The right of appeal is a vested right. Though there is no specific rule in the Code of Criminal Procedure or in the Limitation Act that the appeal or revision is to be filed within specific period, but the convention has been prevailing since the inception of this Court that the appeal is to be filed within 30 days from the date of pronouncement of the judgment or from the date of knowledge. 

 21. 30 days time for preferring appeal to be counted from the date of pronouncement of judgment or date of knowledge of conviction when relevant statutes do no prescribe any date from which limitation is to run. In the instant case the accused petitioner preferred this appeal well within 30 days from the date of his knowledge. 

 22. In the case of a trial alleged to have/been held without the knowledge of the accused and behind his back, the Limitation Act having not provided any special limitation for appeal in case of such trial in absentia as if held ex parte by committing fraud upon the Court by suppressing notice: It would be in consonance with the principle of natural justice that in such an appeal time would run from the day of appellant's knowledge of the judgment as in section 18 of the Limitation Act. Furthermore, extension of time shall always be available if sufficient cause is shown for delay. 

 23. A somewhat similar point came up for decision in the case of Hakim Rai vs State before a Full Bench of Punjab High Court reported in AIR 1957.(Punjab) 134. That was a case concerning complaint filed by a Court for using a forged document in a proceeding before that Court. The complaint was filed in a Court of Additional District Magistrate and it was challenged on appeal before the Court of District Judge. The learned District Judge held the appeal to be barred by limitation and dismissed the same. This dismissal of the appeal as time barred was challenged before the High Court in the case reported on the ground that the appeal was filed within two weeks of his knowledge of the above order of dismissal. Their Lordships of the Full Bench in the above reported case came to a finding thus: 

 "It was an appeal before the District Judge arising out of a criminal proceeding for filing of which the Criminal Procedure Code or the India Limitation Act does not clearly or specifically prescribe any period. In consonance with the principles of natural justice therefore, time in a case like the present would be taken to start from the day of the appellant's knowledge of the filing of the complaint." 

 24. In every case he would be entitled to extension of time on the score of sufficient cause for his inability to file the appeal in time if any specific period is to be supposed to govern the appeal. I would consequently, hold that the appeal of Hakim Rai had been wrongly thrown out as barred by limitation. 

 25. This supports the view I have taken hereinbefore to the effect that for a case where neither the provision of the Criminal Procedure Code nor the Limitation Act clearly prescribe any date from which time would be counted for limitation as to appeal. 30 days' time for appeal would be counted from the date of knowledge of the impugned order of conviction.
